skill.name: error-detective
skill.description: Systematic debugging and error resolution using the TRACE framework for stack traces, root cause analysis, hypothesis testing, and verified fixes.
skill.summary: Guide structured debugging from error capture to verified resolution.
skill.author: AutumnsGrove

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are markdown examples, inline formatting, or local debugging helper behavior rather than malicious execution. I confirmed one medium documentation risk: a Java heap dump example writes to /tmp, which can expose sensitive memory artifacts on shared systems. No prompt injection, data exfiltration intent, or unauthorized network behavior was found.

remediation.issue: Heap dump example uses a shared temporary path.
remediation.suggestion: Change the example to write heap dumps into a private diagnostics directory and add guidance to protect or delete heap files.

remediation.issue: Debug traces and logs can contain sensitive data.
remediation.suggestion: Add a clear reminder to redact tokens, passwords, customer data, and internal host details before sharing diagnostic material.

content.value_statement: Errors are hard to resolve when symptoms hide the real cause. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a structured TRACE workflow for diagnosis and verification.
actual_capabilities: Applies the TRACE framework to capture, read, analyze, check, and execute fixes.
Interprets stack traces for Python, JavaScript, Java, and Go examples.
Classifies common syntax, runtime, logic, integration, and performance errors.
Guides hypothesis testing, reproduction steps, and fix verification.
Includes a local helper script for parsing traces, analyzing logs, and recording debug sessions.
limitations: It cannot access production systems, logs, or repositories unless the user provides access.
It cannot guarantee a root cause when traces, inputs, or environment details are incomplete.
Example fixes may need adaptation for each framework, data model, and deployment policy.
The helper script stores debug notes locally and does not redact sensitive data automatically.

use_cases.title: Resolve production incidents
use_cases.description: Use TRACE to separate symptoms from root causes during API failures, crashes, or outages.

use_cases.title: Debug async UI failures
use_cases.description: Analyze failed requests, promise errors, and inconsistent frontend state before changing code.

use_cases.title: Triage logs and stack traces
use_cases.description: Parse traces, group recurring errors, and document investigation notes for handoff.

prompt_templates.title: Explain This Error
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner triage of a single error message.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Error Detective to explain this error in plain language. Identify the error type, likely cause, and first check I should run.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze a Stack Trace
prompt_templates.scenario: Structured review of a complete trace.
prompt_templates.prompt: Apply the TRACE framework to this stack trace. Separate the root cause from follow-on errors and list the files or functions to inspect first.

prompt_templates.title: Build an Investigation Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a debugging plan for this failure. Include reproduction steps, hypotheses, evidence to collect, and checks that can confirm or reject each hypothesis.

prompt_templates.title: Verify a Production Fix
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced validation before release or rollback.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this proposed fix using Error Detective. Check whether it addresses the root cause, name regression risks, and define verification tests before deployment.

output_examples.input: A cart update fails after an API timeout, and the UI crashes when it reads missing items.
output: Likely root cause: the client assumes every response is successful and shaped like a cart response.
First checks: inspect failed responses, confirm status handling, and verify that error responses do not update cart state.
Fix direction: validate response status and structure before using returned data.

output_examples.input: A Django profile page fails for older accounts that do not have profile records.
output: Likely root cause: existing users were not backfilled when the profile model was added.
First checks: query affected users, confirm missing related records, and review the migration history.
Fix direction: create missing profiles safely and add a guard for future requests.

output_examples.input: A production-only payment failure appears for deleted users with active sessions.
output: Likely root cause: soft-deleted users remain reachable through stale session state.
First checks: compare session data, user deletion state, and repository filtering rules.
Fix direction: filter deleted users and expire sessions when accounts are deleted.

best_practices: Start with the complete error message, stack trace, environment, and reproduction steps.
Change one variable at a time so each test confirms or rejects a specific hypothesis.
Verify the final fix with the original failure path and at least one related regression case.
anti_patterns: Do not patch the visible symptom before identifying the root cause.
Do not ignore warnings, partial failures, or intermittent cases during verification.
Do not paste secrets, tokens, or customer data into traces or logs sent for analysis.

faq.question: What is the TRACE framework?
faq.answer: TRACE means Trace, Read, Analyze, Check, and Execute. It gives a repeatable path from error evidence to verified fix.

faq.question: Can this skill fix code automatically?
faq.answer: It can guide fixes and verification steps. Actual code changes depend on the user, repository access, and tool permissions.

faq.question: Which languages are covered?
faq.answer: The examples cover Python, JavaScript, Java, and Go. The general method also applies to other languages.

faq.question: Does the helper script send logs anywhere?
faq.answer: No evidence of network sending was found. The helper reads local files and stores debug session notes locally.

faq.question: Should I share full production logs?
faq.answer: Share only the needed error context. Redact tokens, passwords, customer data, and internal host details first.

faq.question: When should I use this skill?
faq.answer: Use it when an error needs structured diagnosis, stack trace analysis, root cause isolation, or fix verification.
